risks.risk: Hydraulic leak or inability to hold load (seller’s “tested” not evidenced).
risks.proof: Video: pump up to a working height, release, show it holds for 30–60 seconds; then show underside for any oil seepage.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven to hold load (worst-case: needs service / may leak).

risks.risk: Worn rollers/wheels causing rough travel or uneven fork movement.
risks.proof: Video rolling forward/backward on flat ground plus close-ups of roller tread and any axle play.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worn/unknown condition (worst-case: roller/wheel replacement).

risks.risk: Release valve/pump issues causing jerky lift or poor lowering control.
risks.proof: Video: pump 5–10 strokes, then lower smoothly while keeping forks level; show release lever action.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven to operate smoothly (worst-case: functional problems).

risks.risk: Capacity mismatch due to unclear label text (capacity plate not fully readable).
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the capacity plate/label and any serial/model plate.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case capacity uncertainty (worst-case: not the claimed 2.5 ton).

risks.risk: Missing/damaged parts not visible from one angle (handle, safety components, pump parts, fork condition).
risks.proof: Full photo set: both fork tips, underside/pump area, release lever, all wheels/rollers, and both sides of the frame.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as parts condition unknown (worst-case: missing/damaged components).

proof_requests: Send a short video of the test: lift a known load (or max-rated pallet), hold 30–60 seconds, then lower smoothly; show no dropping and no leaks.
Send clear close-up photos of the capacity plate/label and any brand/serial/model plate.
Send underside/pump-area photos showing seals and any oil seepage.
Send close-ups of all rollers/wheels showing tread condition and any wobble/play.
response.reason: The seller’s statement that it was tested is not verifiable remotely without a video or clear label/serial proof. Photo 0 alone cannot confirm working condition, service history, completeness, or exact capacity, so proof is required before pricing.
